analysis: The PR changes documentation only. It adds a line near cli-reference.md:1025 and a new section in provider-authorization.md at lines 92-107, and bumps the "Last updated" date. The CLI reference units (1ebf05eb42642970:11-13) are unchanged context and I found nothing new there. The new text describes `darkbloom status` and `doctor`: an App Attest lease stays displayed until its `expires_at`, even if the latest renewal arrived more than `snapshotMaxAge` ago. `none` and `legacy` decisions still require receipt within `snapshotMaxAge`. MDM-removal advice, however, requires a matching fresh decision plus `mdm_removal_ready`. `unenroll` re-checks readiness before and after profile inspection. This split keeps the display of a serving lease separate from removal safety, and it fails toward retaining profiles when evidence is stale. That is consistent with T-053 and T-057 (stale authorization, and stranding a provider through premature MDM removal) and with T-052. The description does not make the display equal to a serving grant, so the coordinator-owned authorization and expiry controls are unchanged. No code, endpoint, key, attestation, or encryption behavior changes. Remaining question, not a finding: the implementation (`ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.displayedStatus` and `summary`) and the referenced [platform-current] link are outside the supplied evidence. Whether the code matches this prose, and whether the link definition exists in the file, were not verified. A reviewer of the Swift source should confirm that the displayed-lease path never feeds routing or removal decisions.
